items.body_snippet: POL-1501 (error policy rule): MCP over custom protocols — every agent-facing surface speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 (MCP); a bespoke agent protocol does not ship. — rationale source: mcp-surface.md@51e2228f27e0d7273a3a1bfa80a7499c3c48156e#POL-1501
items.label: POL-1501 (error policy rule): MCP over custom protocols — ev

items.body_snippet: POL-1801 (error policy rule): Event types are four-segment wicked.<domain>.<noun>.<past-tense-verb> — all lowercase, dot-separated, matching the WB-001 pattern; three-segment names are never constructed, statically or dynamically. — rationale source: event-grammar.md@19c1bbcff3efcb1e1f133b474af639162257858e#POL-1801
items.label: POL-1801 (error policy rule): Event types are four-segment w

items.body_snippet: POL-1401 (error policy rule): The embedded durable store (SQLite, ACID/WAL, crash-safe) is the zero-infra default; Postgres is optional behind a feature/profile — the local case never requires a server to run. — rationale source: storage-doctrine.md@33337819b8d43c15fffb320239f9a1013287d4cf#POL-1401
items.label: POL-1401 (error policy rule): The embedded durable store (SQ

items.body_snippet: POL-1704 (critical policy rule): Every graph store must pass the GraphStore conformance suite before it ships — the suite is the gate, the contract doc is the rationale; a store that skips the suite does not merge. — rationale source: engine-contract.md@be5d01b04e720ed44c9f69eca18e07febf8f2a61#POL-1704
items.label: POL-1704 (critical policy rule): Every graph store must pass

items.body_snippet: POL-2002 (critical policy rule): The verdict is the verdict — conformance, bake-off, benchmark, and gate results never change based on who runs them or how urgent the moment is; a NO-GO is a NO-GO for everyone. — rationale source: universal-donts.md@e42f2fbea0217b0978f878f6ae4dad7ab36387bc#POL-2002
items.label: POL-2002 (critical policy rule): The verdict is the verdict

items.body_snippet: POL-1301 (critical policy rule): Every cross-plane interaction goes through the owning plane's contract, never around it: experience reaches control only via crew's public `/api/v1` + WS, control drives capability only as governed workers over workflows-as-data, and capability reaches the foundation only through garden's skills (estate MCP, vault/ledger evidence, bus events). — rationale source: plane-boundaries.md@d4924f167b1f7b120b076c26bac6e492e8ddbdbb#POL-1301

items.body_snippet: POL-1802 (warn policy rule): Producer domains are whitelisted: qe, crew, garden, interactive (bus SPEC live-domain list) plus estate (governance lifecycle events, wicked-core AW-22); the `test` namespace survives only as the legacy-stable QE-lifecycle spelling emitted under the qe domain column. A new producer domain lands in the bus SPEC catalog before its first emit. — rationale source: event-grammar.md@19c1bbcff3efcb1e1f133b474af639162257858e#POL-1802
items.label: POL-1802 (warn policy rule): Producer domains are whiteliste

items.body_snippet: PAT-1502 (error pattern rule): Rules are read-only over MCP: recall surfaces exist (rules.recall, RulesInventory, knowledge.recall), a write surface deliberately does not — the absence of a rules.write tool is the guardrail (see estate POL-1101 / ADR-012 for the authorship contract). — rationale source: mcp-surface.md@51e2228f27e0d7273a3a1bfa80a7499c3c48156e#PAT-1502
